messages:
tara: Heads-up — after the NF4/FP4 mass rollout last night we have a clear regression on a subset of hosts: sustained throughput drop (~35%) and KV cache memory spike leading to OOM evictions on the 4bit kernel path.

mike: ugh. which pool/hosts? do we have graphs?

tara: us-west-2-gpu-3 pool. grafana: https://grafana.redwood/shot/abcd1234 (RPS/latency/kv_mem). quick log snippet: 
```
2026-03-17T22:12:34Z host=us-west-2-gpu-3 kernel=4bit_v2 schedule=dynamic batch_target=32 kv_cache_mb=18432 throughput_rps=420 -> 270 errors=0
2026-03-17T22:12:40Z host=us-west-2-gpu-3 kernel=4bit_v2 kv_evictions=512 slab_frag=0.23 malloc_failures=3
```

cheng: initial hunch: kernel selector may have switched to a slow path for small prefix lengths due to mixed-precision fallback. Could also be batching heuristics increasing batch size beyond efficient regime causing KV cache churn.

sara: telemetry dump (1h) shows spike around 22:10 with avg batch size up from 6->18 and sampling window increase. Maybe autoscaler bumped instance density and scheduler didn't account for increased tail-latency -> batching picked bigger microbatches.

kevin: I'll run a profiling snapshot on one host. landing perftrace now: `perf-trace --host us-west-2-gpu-3 --pid 3241 --duration 60s --tags kernel,kv,batching`

infra-bot: deploy-bot triggered: rollback_flag set for model=redwood/aldor-4bit@canary on pool=us-west-2-gpu; reason=kv_mem_spike. See /deploys/rollback/2334567889

mike: good. we should bisect whether 4bit_v2 kernel change or scheduler heuristics change is culprit. Two parallel checks: 1) force kernel->4bit_v1 on host and monitor; 2) revert batching-window heuristic and observe.

tara: agree. plan: (A) hotfix: force older kernel on affected hosts (RKERNEL_FORCE=4bit_v1) and lower batch_target to 8; (B) collect microprofiles for both kernel variants; (C) run offline calibration test to check perf/accuracy delta.

cheng: adding probe hooks: `telemetry.sample({host, kernel, batch, kv_mem, lat_p50, lat_p95}, interval=10s)` — please keep running for 30m. Also collect KV slab histograms: `kvctl histogram --host us-west-2-gpu-3 > /tmp/kv_hist.json`

mike: after forcing 4bit_v1 on one host I saw throughput recover to ~410 rps and kv_mem decrease by ~20%. initial numbers look promising.

kevin: profiling results attached (short): 
```
# profile 4bit_v2 (slow)
kernel_dispatch_ms: 14.3
attention_kernel_ms: 28.7
kv_lookup_ms: 9.6
memcpy_host_ms: 12.2
batch_serialize_ms: 6.5

# profile 4bit_v1 (fast)
kernel_dispatch_ms: 10.1
attention_kernel_ms: 21.0
kv_lookup_ms: 6.1
memcpy_host_ms: 6.8
batch_serialize_ms: 5.9
```

kevin: notable: memcpy_host and attention kernel are both ~2x slower on v2. Also kv_lookup increased — suggests different memory layout / quant packing in v2 causing worse locality.

tara: sounds like a robust repro. v2's quant packing change (packed lanes) likely increased random-access slices in KV cache, increasing memory pressure and memcpy overhead.

mike: action items: 1) rollback kernel->v1 on production pool until we ship a patched v2; 2) open PR to revert packing change and add microbench tests for kv locality; 3) add scheduler guardrail to cap batch_target when average prefix_len < 64 to avoid inefficient large microbatches; 4) add canary that monitors kv_evictions and slab_frag in real time with alert threshold 5% above baseline.

tara: I'm creating the incident doc and postmortem checklist. putting owners: mike (kernel rollback + PR), cheng (scheduler guardrail), kevin (profiling + regression tests), sara (telemetry + alerts), ops-bot (followup runbook).

ops-bot: incident created: https://incidents.redwood/INC-2026-2334 — severity: S2 — timeline pinned.

mike: quick reproducible test we used locally: 
```
# reproduce locally
export RKERNEL=4bit_v2
python perf_runner.py --model aldor --batch-pattern 'small->burst' --prefix-dist 'short' --kv-size 16000
# observe kv_evictions and rps drop
```

cheng: extra note: calibration step for v2 changed thresholds that select FP fallback for small layers; that could cause mixed execution (some ops FP32) and blow up compute cost. add unit test to validate per-layer quant correctness.

sara: for the canary tomorrow I'll schedule a staggered rollout with 5% of traffic and explicit monitor for kv_evictions, p95 > 2x, and avg_batch > 12. If any trigger, auto-disable 4bit_v2.

tara: thanks all. mike please post PR link and rollback hash here when ready. keep the thread for timeline/notes. :thumbsup:

mike: PR opened: https://git.redwood/repo/patches/4567 — rollback patch + regression test included. rolling via canary now.

kevin: will follow up with microbench summary and recommended patch for packed-lane layout next 24h.

infra-bot: canary status: pool=us-west-2-gpu-3 pct=5% -> healthy after rollback. monitoring: kv_evictions down to baseline.

tara: closing loop: we need a postmortem that calls out kernel packing tradeoff, missing locality benchmark, and missing scheduler guardrail. assign follow-ups in the postmortem doc.

ops-bot: incident INC-2026-2334 updated: status=stabilized owners=[mike,cheng,kevin,sara] next_update=2026-03-18T10:00:00Z
